title: Newton's Identities: Power Sums and Elementary Symmetric Polynomials

problemStatement.formal: Newton identities express power sums p_k in terms of elementary symmetric polynomials e_j, and conversely.
problemStatement.plain: Formalize Newton identities for two, three, and four variables, including recursive and closed-form power-sum identities plus inversion formulas.
whyMatters: Connects Vieta-style coefficient formulas to symmetric functions and trace invariants
Provides executable polynomial-identity proofs using ring and field_simp

proven: Newton identities are verified for 2, 3, and 4 variables with 31 public theorems in the primary file.
Inversion formulas recover elementary symmetric polynomials from power sums over fields.
Application identities cover discriminants, matrix-trace coefficients, and the sum-of-cubes factorization.
open: Generalize the case-by-case proofs to arbitrary n using Mathlib symmetric-polynomial infrastructure.
Formalize broader algorithms such as Faddeev-LeVerrier from the same identities.
knownResults.goal: Move from verified finite-variable identities toward a general Newton identity theorem.

currentState.focus: Verified source-backed record: primary proof has 383 lines, 31 public theorems, 0 axioms, and 0 sorries.
currentState.nextAction: Optional follow-on: prove a general arbitrary-n Newton identities theorem.
